name: Biotin

lead: Biotin (vitamin B7) is a water-soluble B vitamin that serves as a coenzyme in fatty acid, glucose and amino acid metabolism. It is widely sold in high-dose supplements marketed for hair, skin and nails.

True biotin deficiency, which can cause hair thinning and a scaly rash, is rare. In people with normal intake, the evidence that supplements improve hair growth is weak and rests mostly on small, low-quality studies and case reports.

paras: Biotin is a cofactor for carboxylase enzymes involved in keratin-related and energy metabolism. When a deficiency exists, replacing it restores normal hair growth, but there is no good evidence that intake beyond requirements boosts follicle activity.

Biotin is generally well tolerated, but high doses interfere with many laboratory immunoassays, including troponin and thyroid tests, which can produce falsely high or low results; the FDA has issued warnings. It is sold as a supplement. Anyone planning blood tests should disclose use to their clinician.
